newsitem.title: USA: OCC to waive fees on new banks in low-income areas.
newsitem.headline: OCC to waive fees on new banks in low-income areas.

text.p: - U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said on Monday that his office will waive fees for new banks in low- and moderate-income areas to help reach out for the 12 million American households that he said do not have access to banking or financial services.
"I am announcing a policy change that will encourage national banks to locate in underserved communities," Ludwig told a conference of the Consumer Bankers Association (CBA).
"The OCC is waiving fees for applications for new charters and branches in low- and moderate-income census tracts not currently served by a depository institutions," he added.
The bank regulator also said the OCC will convene a forum this winter to study ways to reach out for Americans without existing access or relationships with financial institutions.
"We don't really know much about why they choose not to participate in the banking system," he added.
Among Americans who do not have access to or do not use financial industry services, Ludwig cited minority families, young Americans, and new and small entrepreneurs.

"They include the working poor," Ludwig stressed, adding 16 percent of American families earning between $10,000 and $25,000 use non-bank businesses to cash paychecks. "By the year 2010, one-third of the U.S. population will be minority."
Broader availability of banking services would dovetail with the U.S. Treasury's plan to make all federal payments available by electronic transfers by 1999, Ludwig said.

"There are reasons why banking has not addressed the needs of (certain market segments) before," Ludwig said, citing the banking industry's reluctance to accept innovation and the costs involved with serving a non-mainstream market.
Ludwig said initiatives within the banking industry such as the CBA conference and technology developments were key elements in addressing the issue.
